findings.evidence: Inventory and the decision table skip https://github.com/vitorpamplona/amethyst/pull/4186 with reason “DECK reader work has no verified Nostr protocol or event surface,” but the exact title is “Implement DECK-0003 (SNO) reader, rasterizer, and Cyberspace bag opening.” No PR body is supplied, so the Nostr-negative hard-gate claim is not source-grounded here.
findings.recommendation: Re-read the #4186 body and confirm whether Cyberspace bag opening emits or consumes Nostr events before keeping the skip; if a protocol surface exists, fold or include it instead.
findings.title: Amethyst #4186 skip is not independently confirmable from the snapshot

findings.evidence: https://github.com/vitorpamplona/amethyst/pull/4185 is titled “refactor: Render/Display split, batches 1–3 — shared displays for AccountViewModel-bound composables,” yet late_delta_review_2026-09-23.md gives it the same reason as the marmot PRs: “MLS optional fields, supported extensions and desktop group rendering.” The draft Amethyst in-dev story cites 4187/4182/4184/4188/4189 and not 4185.

findings.title: Decision-memo “undeployed runtime” overreaches for nostter

findings.title: NIP-34 and app-discovery skips are conservative; announcement bodies not supplied

verdict.summary: Late-cutoff dispositions cover all 37 inventory PR identities and both fips2go tags; the three in-dev groups are distinct and the draft does not treat them as tagged/deployed releases; fips2go 0.6.1/0.7.0 caveats appear in the draft. This is not the final ten-family source-pass or exact-ledger gate: PR/release bodies and full collector artifacts were not in the snapshot, so several skip/caveat claims still need a primary-body re-read.
